models_evaluated: U-Net with residual backbone (multi-physician models MD1-7 and MD1-6; individual-physician models)

links.outcome: Effect of inter-physician variation in reference segmentations on auto-segmentation model Dice performance
links.effect: Model trained on MD7 (highest edge roughness 0.106) had lower Dice than MD6 (58.5±15.8% vs 67.1±16.8%, p<0.001). Including MD7 data gave 7 cases with Dice ≤40% versus 4 without MD7.
links.quote: This study demonstrates that there is significant variation in style and quality in manual segmentations in clinical care, and that training AI auto-segmentation algorithms from real-world, clinical datasets may result in unexpectedly under-performing algorithms with the inclusion of outliers.

unlisted_practices: Filter clinical training data using a slice-to-slice inconsistency metric (edge roughness) to remove low-quality physician segmentations
Compare models trained on multiple versus individual physicians' segmentations

screen.reason: The study investigates how physician variation in clinical training labels affects AI auto-segmentation performance and tests a data-curation practice (filtering out inconsistent annotators using an edge-roughness metric) to improve model robustness.

primary.practice: training data quality filtering based on physician inconsistency metrics
